microtheory.name: discourse_analysis
microtheory.definition: Language above the sentence level — cohesion, coherence, narrative structure, dialogue, text types. How utterances combine into meaningful larger units. Halliday + Hasan's cohesion; Rhetorical Structure Theory (Mann + Thompson); narrative structure (Labov, Propp). Substrate analogue: how substrate's individual Messages combine into ongoing dialogue or narrative.

concepts.name: cohesion
concepts.definition: Halliday + Hasan 1976. Surface ties between sentences — pronouns, conjunctions, lexical repetition. Substrate analogue: substrate's inter-Message reference links.

concepts.name: coherence
concepts.definition: Underlying meaning relations between parts of discourse. Some discourses cohere without surface cohesion + vice versa. Substrate analogue: substrate's semantic-coherence of Message sequence.

concepts.name: referential_chain
concepts.definition: Same entity referred to repeatedly with varying expressions ('John... he... the boy... that idiot'). Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent-entity tracking.

concepts.name: lexical_cohesion
concepts.definition: Repetition + synonymy + collocation across sentences holding text together. Substrate analogue: substrate's repeated-Concept activation.

concepts.name: conjunction
concepts.definition: Words signaling relationships between sentences. Additive (and), adversative (but), causal (because), temporal (then). Substrate analogue: substrate's inter-Message relation markers.

concepts.name: rhetorical_structure_theory
concepts.definition: Mann + Thompson 1988. Text as hierarchy of nucleus-satellite relations: elaboration, contrast, cause, evidence, etc. Substrate analogue: substrate's hierarchical discourse Term-tree.

concepts.name: centering_theory
concepts.definition: Grosz + Joshi + Weinstein 1995. Local coherence through entity-tracking; transitions classified by preserved vs shifted center. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-step entity-focus.

concepts.name: topic_structure
concepts.definition: What the discourse is about + how it shifts. Topic chains, topic decay. Substrate analogue: substrate's current-Mt evolution through dialogue.

concepts.name: narrative_structure
concepts.definition: Labov + Waletzky 1967. Abstract → orientation → complicating action → evaluation → resolution → coda. Substrate analogue: substrate's event-sequence-as-narrative.

concepts.name: propp_narrative_functions
concepts.definition: Propp 1928. Russian folktales analyzed into 31 functions in fixed sequence. Substrate analogue: substrate's narrative-grammar template.

concepts.name: story_grammar
concepts.definition: Mandler + Johnson 1977. Setting + episodes + resolution. Hierarchical structure aids comprehension + memory. Substrate analogue: substrate's hierarchical event encoding.

concepts.name: dialogue_structure
concepts.definition: Multi-party language organized around turn-taking, adjacency pairs, sequences, repair. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-Message dialogue with role exchange.

concepts.name: sequence_organization
concepts.definition: Schegloff. How talk gets organized into recognizable sequences with first-pair-parts + second-pair-parts. Substrate analogue: substrate's question-answer + greeting-greeting + offer-acceptance structures.

concepts.name: preference_organization
concepts.definition: Some second-pair-parts (acceptances of offers, agreements) are preferred + come quickly; others (refusals, disagreements) are dispreferred + delayed. Substrate analogue: substrate's response-latency conditioning.

concepts.name: genre
concepts.definition: Recognizable text type. Narrative, exposition, argument, instruction, news report. Each with conventions. Substrate analogue: substrate's discourse-mode Mt.

concepts.name: register
concepts.definition: Variation in language by situation. Formal/informal, technical/casual. Substrate analogue: substrate's contextual lexical+grammatical adjustment.

concepts.name: style
concepts.definition: Recurrent linguistic choices distinguishing individuals or groups. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-instance characteristic patterns.

concepts.name: discourse_marker
concepts.definition: Words signaling discourse function: 'well', 'so', 'you know', 'I mean'. Substrate analogue: substrate's discourse-state signaling.

concepts.name: information_structure
concepts.definition: Topic vs comment, given vs new, focus + presupposition. Affects intonation + syntax. Substrate analogue: substrate's known-vs-novel partitioning of Message content.

concepts.name: focus
concepts.definition: Most informative part of utterance. Often prosodically prominent + syntactically marked. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-attention Concept within Message.

concepts.name: given_information
concepts.definition: What's already in common ground. Often pronominalized + de-stressed. Substrate analogue: substrate's already-known Concept marker.

concepts.name: topic_continuity
concepts.definition: Givon. How long an entity stays topical. Measured by gap-to-next-mention. Substrate analogue: substrate's entity-attention persistence.

concepts.name: implicational_scale
concepts.definition: Coherence relations ordered: identity > paraphrase > elaboration > exemplification. Substrate analogue: substrate's hierarchy of inter-Message relations.

concepts.name: common_ground_update
concepts.definition: Stalnaker. Each successful utterance adds to common ground. Substrate analogue: substrate's shared-context monotonic accumulation.

concepts.name: narrative_perspective
concepts.definition: First-person vs third-person, internal vs external. Affects what's accessible to narrator. Substrate analogue: substrate's perspective-conditioned narration.

rules.name: coherence_requires_inferable_relations
rules.head: the substrate processes sequential utterances
rules.body: they must be related by some inferable relation (elaboration, contrast, cause, etc.) for the discourse to cohere. Substrate's inter-Message coherence.

rules.name: referential_chains_track_entities
rules.head: the substrate processes a multi-utterance discourse
rules.body: it tracks each entity across multiple references via various expressions. Pronouns, definite descriptions. Substrate's persistent-entity model.

rules.name: narrative_follows_schema
rules.head: the substrate processes narrative discourse
rules.body: the structure follows the genre template (abstract → orientation → complication → resolution). Substrate's narrative-mode parsing.

rules.name: topic_shifts_signal_segment_boundaries
rules.head: the substrate detects a topic shift
rules.body: the shift signals a discourse-segment boundary. Substrate's segmentation cue.

rules.name: common_ground_grows_monotonically
rules.head: the substrate has a successful dialogue exchange
rules.body: the common ground expands monotonically; entities + propositions accumulate. Substrate's shared-context update.
